hardware.variant: One operator-reported ESP-Mosaico R5 V1.2 kit.

scenario: On one R5 V1.2 device, fetch the public package catalog over HTTP and HTTPS, then separately exercise the target Spark worker against a local Responses fixture using a synthetic image. Start the Workshop GUI.
expected: Both catalog downloads succeed with identical bytes; the fixture accepts the worker's model-list and response requests and validates the synthetic PNG and step context.
observed: The anonymous catalog GET returned HTTP 200 over both HTTP and HTTPS, 2,156 bytes each, with identical SHA-256 ca9a3620ca49a3b01869a7a43415f099e5746c6be8b37fd2bd6794de80b34e00. HTTPS peer and host verification were enabled with the public ISRG Root X2 certificate. Separately, the target worker received HTTP 200 for GET /v1/models and POST /v1/responses from a local fixture. The fixture received a synthetic 640×480 PNG (972 bytes), checked step 2 title/instruction and the PNG data URI, and returned its explicit FIXTURE RESPONSE marker. The Workshop GUI process was started and Home was displayed; no physical Ask interaction was confirmed at recording time.
limits: The package-catalog HTTP/HTTPS check and local Responses-fixture worker check were separate operations.
The fixture test used only a synthetic image and an explicit fixture response; it does not establish a live model response or an Ask-button interaction.
No user photograph, credential or private endpoint was recorded. The GUI was running at Home, but physical Ask interaction remained unconfirmed.
